packages.headline: God of War Laufey Delayed to May 2027

sources.label: IGN Games
sources.evidenceText:
God of War Laufey will no longer be released in February, as Sony Santa Monica has pushed it back to May 2027.
God of War Laufey Delayed to May 2027
The game will now launch on May 20, 2027, with the studio stating that it needs more time to make a product that meets fans' expectations. Sony Santa Monica also confirmed it would share more details on the game soon. It's possible we'll see something at The Game Awards, but there could also be a new State of Play before the end of the year (or very early 2027) that may reveal more about the next God of War installment.
An update regarding God of War Laufey's release date. https://t.co/qCw9O3dqtR
God of War Laufey had previously been slated to release on February 16, 2027. This window has become exceptionally crowded, especially after some games like Fable pivoted from a fall 2026 release to early 2027 to avoid the blast zone of GTA 6 . This will not only give God of War some space to breathe, but potentially allow other games to stretch their wings that may not be as high on the priority list for gamers compared to a new first-party PlayStation game.
God of War Laufey has been met with no shortage of skepticism and criticism from some gamers , partially due to the fact that Kratos has been sidelined as the main character. As a result, it will be important for Santa Monica Studio to be on their A-game and deliver something exceptional. If there's anything that falls short of expectations, the internet will ruthlessly pick it apart, regardless of it's actually fair to do so.
God of War Laufey will be one of the biggest games of 2027, as it will continue the story Sony Santa Monica set in motion back in 2018. Although Laufey is the protagonist, it is expected to overlap and connect back to the last two games, with Kratos also having a role in the new one. It's unclear what kind of larger implications and ramifications God of War Laufey will have on this universe, but it seems like a pretty significant expansion of the franchise . A new Kratos-led God of War title is also actively in the works .

packages.headline: Bringing Jin Sakai back to life for Ghost of Yōtei: Most Wanted

sources.label: PlayStation Blog
sources.evidenceText:
Behind the scenes of the art, animation, and more that went into bringing back the Ghost of Tsushima as a playable character.
Bringing Jin Sakai back to life for Ghost of Yōtei: Most Wanted
It’s been amazing to watch the response to Ghost of Yōtei Complete Edition , from photo mode shots to Echoes of Sekigahara* reactions to flawless fights against Nobushige and beyond. But some of our favorite videos we’ve seen since launch feature Jin Sakai in Most Wanted*, and we’ve loved watching people tear through bounties as the returning Ghost of Tsushima.
With all of these great new moments featuring Jin, we wanted to dive into a little bit of the process behind bringing him back for Ghost of Yōtei, including all the tiny details that help make him feel like himself. Here’s some insight from some members of our team who helped bring him back to life.
How Most Wanted opened the door for Jin’s return
With Most Wanted our goal was to create a new way to experience Ghost of Yotei’s combat. We were excited to focus on challenge and mastery in a highly replayable format.
We wanted to give players new opportunities to grow stronger and master specific forms of combat, building on the foundation established in the main campaign. Very quickly the idea of a class-based, roguelike model emerged as a path to achieve these goals and as an opportunity to experience combat from perspectives other than only Atsu.
As the team got excited about the idea, plenty of production and logistical questions emerged about what would be possible. We thought Jin Sakai would fit perfectly in this mode, but we wanted to make sure we could deliver an experience that was authentic to his character. During the initial prototyping of Most Wanted, we started with other characters to prove out the idea and get a better understanding of what would be necessary to bring Jin back.

packages.headline: Escape Academy 2: Back 2 School – Become a Valedictorian with These Tips

sources.label: Xbox Wire
sources.evidenceText:
Cram a little early studying in to start the school year off right with these tips for Escape Academy 2: Back 2 School, available November 5 on Game Pass
Escape Academy 2: Back 2 School – Become a Valedictorian with These Tips
Fortunately, Escape Academy 2: Back 2 School fills a great niche: providing a mountain of puzzles, but with clear structure, unobtrusive in-game hints, and a colorful, family-friendly, punny presentation that’s perfect for enjoying with anyone in local or online co-op (but can be played entirely solo if that’s your bag). It’s available November 5, 2026 for XBOX Series X|S and XBOX on PC, as well as day one with XBOX Game Pass.
Like the original Escape Academy , Back 2 School features lots of discrete, timed and graded escape rooms, which are delightfully free from the constraints of budget, space and physics that limit their real-world counterparts. New for the sequel, however, is that between rooms you can explore the Escape Academy campus directly as a progressively expanding hub world, which is itself full of puzzles to solve and secrets to find.
For a certain kind of gamer, nothing lights them up more than the promise of a big space full of environmental puzzles. Puzzles can be tricky to make accessible, though, presenting a thin line sometimes between childishly easy and frustratingly difficult.
I really liked this balance between the intensity of the timed escape rooms and the more low-pressure puzzle solving and exploration between them. Connecting up the escape rooms with an interactive, puzzle-filled environment instead of clicking through a menu of static images really elevates the whole experience.

packages.headline: From Polish Museums to XBOX: Bringing the World of The End of the Sun to Life

sources.label: Xbox Wire
sources.evidenceText:
Some of the quests in The End of the Sun began in an unusual way - with objects we discovered in small museums across Poland. Sometimes, an old tool or a How history and fact were woven into the folklore behind The End of the Sun.
From Polish Museums to XBOX: Bringing the World of The End of the Sun to Life
Some of the quests in The End of the Sun began in an unusual way – with objects we discovered in small museums across Poland. Sometimes, an old tool or a fascinating piece of traditional craftsmanship inspired us so much that we decided to build part of the game’s story around it.
When we first started creating The End of the Sun , a first-person adventure inspired by Slavic folklore, we wanted to build a world that would do more than tell an engaging story. We wanted it to feel truly alive, with every building, object, and detail having its own history.
As a Slavic sorcerer investigating the mystery of an abandoned village, you enter a world inspired by Polish culture, ancient beliefs, and traditions rarely explored in video games. To bring that world to life, we decided to look beyond our computer screens and explore the real places where pieces of this history are still preserved.
From Polish Museums to a Living Game World
One of the most important techniques we used was photogrammetry, which allowed us to bring real-world objects directly into the game as detailed 3D models.
We partnered with local ethnographic museums in Poland, including the Open-Air Museum in Szymbark and the Grociarnia Ethnographic Museum in Jastrzębia. Thanks to their support, we were able to scan hundreds of historical objects, including entire buildings.
We’ve always believed that we’re surrounded by remarkable cultural heritage worth sharing, and creating The End of the Sun gave us an opportunity to introduce some of it to players around the world.

packages.headline: How The Challenge Shrine Will Change How you Play Halls of Torment

sources.label: Xbox Wire
sources.evidenceText:
Hello, adventurers! The Lost Archives, the second DLC forHalls of Torment, is available now on XBOX! There’s also a large and free update for all All the details on the new DLC with gameplay tips for Halls of Torment.
How The Challenge Shrine Will Change How you Play Halls of Torment
The Lost Archives , the second DLC for Halls of Torment, is available now on XBOX! There’s also a large and free update for all players.From the swamps of our first DLC, the Boglands , we are marching into The Lost Archives , where cultists and forgotten knowledge await us.
You’re a new tormented Soul? Here’s a quick overview.
Halls of Torment is a horde survival game with roguelite elements, made in the style of the late-90s action RPGs: pre-rendered graphics, dark dungeons and lots of loot.
Set 30 minutes aside, pick a hero and try to survive as wave after wave of monsters closes in. You can take full control of your hero or use automatic attacks. What’s truly important are your choices: abilities, traits and items that can turn a good build into an unstoppable one. In the depths the Tormented Lords are awaiting, unique bosses that dominate their halls.
Between runs, quests unlock new heroes, abilities, items and blessings that make you permanently stronger, so every attempt takes you a bit further, even when you don’t make it out alive.
The Lost Archives adds a new hall and two new heroes: the Inquisitor, who maintains an iron defense with a harsh focus on retribution and judgement, and the Blood Apostle, who sacrifices her own health for immense gains. Each comes with new abilities, upgrades for existing ones and three full sets of equipment, opening up entirely new combinations.
Both heroes take existing mechanics and push them further. The Inquisitor heralds Block, Defense and Retribution, with several new Retribution items. It introduces two new mechanics: Judgement and Execution. Whenever the Inquisitor takes damage, he puts Judgement on all enemies around him, while his mace triggers Executions. Judgement stacks spread between enemies until they are triggered, then deal unblockable damage, a great way to get rid of strong enemies hiding in a swarm.

packages.headline: Indie Selects for November 2026: Survive and Thrive

sources.label: Xbox Wire
sources.evidenceText:
This November, the ID@XBOX team is thankful for six standout Indie Selects that invite you to survive unbelievable horrors, live your best life, and sometimes do a little of both.
Indie Selects for November 2026: Survive and Thrive
Every Wednesday, dive into the Indie Select Hub — your gateway to a fresh, curated indie collection plus four themed spotlights that rotate weekly! You can always find this collection hub in the XBOX Store and on XBOX.com/IndieSelects.
The holiday season is just around the corner, and the ID@XBOX team is excited to share November’s Indie Selects! Think this is our last Monthly Selects of the year? Think again. Stay tuned next month for our first-ever December Selects, with plenty of indie games to add to your wish list, whether you’re asking Santa or just dropping not-so-subtle hints to your roommate.
This November, we’re thankful for six standout Indie Selects that invite you to survive unbelievable horrors, live your best life, and sometimes do a little of both. Do you slay the undead by the dozen, or put them to work as a surprisingly productive agricultural workforce? Do you prefer solving puzzles surrounded by vibrant colors or unspeakable nightmare fuel? And that sound you hear? Maybe there’s a killer after you. Or maybe the rhythm is going to get you.
Whether you’re not quite ready to let go of Halloween or just looking for something that matches your unique vibe, here are this month’s Indie Selects (in no particular order):
Outside of its odes to Resident Evil and Twin Peaks, Silver Pines has borrowed some of the most innovative features seen in modern gaming to deliver a highly polished survival horror experience. It has Silent Hill ’s map annotations, Gears of War ’s active reload, and most notably, Prince of Persia: The Lost Crown ’s photo system. If you find a boarded-up door but don’t yet have the crowbar, or a cryptic clue for which you haven’t found the puzzle, you can use your in-game camera (you play as a detective after all) to take a photo which will be pinned to your map. This makes backtracking when you find the necessary item so satisfying, as you work through your own visual to-do list. It’s a feature that should be mandatory for all Metroidvanias moving forwards.
Wych Elm, the ex-Arrowhead developers, opted for rotoscoping to give their protagonists, NPCs and enemies a unique aesthetic that fits perfectly with the unsettling town they have built for you to explore. The gameplay takes place on beautifully drawn 2D scenes which have routes towards and away from the camera, allowing you to explore an intricate, interconnected 3D map which encourages and rewards exploration.
Silver Pines is the best survival horror game you will play this year. packages.headline: FromSoftware's Bloodborne Is Still Selling Hundreds of Thousands of Copies, Over a Decade After Launch

sources.label: IGN Games
sources.evidenceText:
All FromSoftware games rule, but Bloodborne has the coolest vibes. Perhaps it shouldn't come as a surprise, then, that it's still selling hundreds of thousands of copies a year despite being over a decade old.
FromSoftware's Bloodborne Is Still Selling Hundreds of Thousands of Copies, Over a Decade After Launch
All FromSoftware games rule, but Bloodborne has the coolest vibes. You’re dripping in Victorian garb, flanked by gothic architecture, and stalked by Lovecraftian terrors across cobbled streets that run red with each sword swing, wielding weapons that shift and transform mid-combo, parrying with a shotgun — it’s just sick. Perhaps it shouldn't come as a surprise, then, that it's still selling hundreds of thousands of copies a year despite being over a decade old.
According to Alinea Analytics estimates, the PS4 exclusive has reportedly sold more than 251,000 copies this year alone. Analyst Rhys Elliott took to social media to note that the game has sold to an estimated 10.4 million copies since going on sale in March 2015, generating around $317 million in revenue.
On top of the impressive sales, an estimated half a million played Bloodborne in October through PS Plus, Sony’s video game subscription service. Bloodborne continues to be hugely popular among fans of FromSoftware games, the data suggests. Of those nearly 500,000 players, 12% also played Elden Ring this month, while 6% also played Dark Souls 3 and 5% also played Sekiro. “There’s a cohort of gamers who are always bouncing between different From games. Can’t blame them, especially with this one," Elliott said.
Bloodborne is one of the few PS4 exclusives that never got a PS5 update and is still (officially at least) locked at 30fps, despite public demand for a Bloodborne remaster. Modders have managed to get Bloodborne running at 120fps on higher resolutions than previously possible on PS5 , however.
The now-shuttered Bluepoint , the studio behind the successful Shadow of the Colossus and Demon's Souls remakes, reportedly pitched a Bloodborne remake last year that was rejected not by Sony, as many had thought, but by FromSoftware itself.
Bloodborne's status has long been in limbo, with various individuals with ties to the project sharing conflicting thoughts on what can be made of it. Back in 2024 , FromSoftware director Hidetaka Miyazaki said it was "not in my place" to talk about a Bloodborne remake because FromSoftware does not own the IP. He also told Eurogamer at the time that the game would benefit from a release on modern hardware .
Then, the following year, PlayStation's Shuhei Yoshida offered a theory on KindaFunny as to what was going on with Bloodborne that might have matched up with what happened to Bluepoint's pitch: "Bloodborne has always been the most asked thing. And people wonder why we haven’t really done anything, even an update or a remaster. Should be easy, right? The company is known for doing so many remasters, right, some people get frustrated.

GTA 6 Rakes in Over $750 Million in Preorders 2 Weeks Ahead of Release Date
GTA 6 launches in just two short weeks. It’s one of the most highly anticipated video game releases of all time and possibly the biggest pop culture phenomenon of this decade.
For reference, GTA 5 made $800 million in its first 24 hours , and reached $1 billion in three days , making it the fastest entertainment product to reach $1 billion in history. It's possible that GTA 6 blows past this record, given what we're already seeing, but only time will tell once November 19 actually gets here.
The Standard Edition of GTA 6 isn’t a whole lot cheaper. At $80, the base game also costs players a pretty penny — something that Zelnick told IGN was a reflection of the game’s value and actually a “bargain.”
GTA 6 releases on November 19, 2026 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox X|S. For more interesting stats about the game, check out IGN’s report on how many players intend to take off work on release day, or see the concerning amount of fans who would give up their pets for a month for the chance to play it a week early.
The hype for this particular entry is off the charts, and fans of Rockstar’s open-world action-adventure franchise are putting their money where their mouths are. According to data aggregated by Sensor Tower , Rockstar has already made three-quarters of the way to a billion dollars in preorders alone.

World of Warcraft Forever launch day live blog.
World of Warcraft Forever Launch Live Blog: It's Looking Like a Smooth Blizzard Launch
World of Warcraft Forever is finally here, and the gates to this alternate version of Azeroth open at 3 PM PST / 6 PM EST. All the signs from the beta are pointing to Forever being one of the biggest launches in Warcraft history, with so many people testing the game that developers claimed it put up "the craziest numbers" they've seen in 17 years.
Even after expanding the level cap in the beta, it was still capped at level 30, and most people – outside of some promotions – had to buy an expensive Skyborne pack to get in. Once the live servers go up, the only barrier to playing WoW Forever is going to be an active WoW subscription or a friend code. (And there are going to be a lot of friend codes out there.)
But while WoW Forever promises to be a huge launch and a return to form for many WoW fans, the real test is going to be how well the servers hold up. I've been playing Blizzard's games my entire life, and it's pretty much a given that something is going to go wrong when Blizzard flicks the switch to open up the game. Even last week, when Blizzard opened its name reservation system, European players couldn't get in for hours, and American players were greeted with long server queues and disconnects. So, I expect the full launch to be, well, spicy.
World of Warcraft Forever Live Blog
8:15 pm: Even a couple hours in, it seems like World of Warcraft Forever is the smoothest Blizzard launch in years. Even after the pain that the servers felt when name reservations went live last week, everything seems pretty buttoned up. I'm seeing fewer and fewer people having problems getting into the game, and the issues now seem limited to folks getting frustrated at faction limits and the sheer amount of people competing for mobs.
7:43 pm: I'm finally on the way to Brill, and as soon as I got past the gate, I rounded a corner, and got blown away by some incredible lighting. Blizzard really did knock the graphics upgrades out of the park with WoW Forever. If you have powerful enough hardware, trust me, max the game out, at least for a little bit.
Just speaking anecdotally, but there were so many Undead players that I had to group up with four other people to finish one of the first quests. But, that's exactly what Forever's devs want you to do.
But I'm going to be in the trenches, trying to get in myself and keeping an eye on the community to find all the cool stuff people are talking about, and gathering all of that here. So, whether you're stuck at work while the servers go up, or you're inevitably frustrated by the servers buckling under the weight of millions of MMO fans, stay tuned for all the fun.
